clue.text: I hold my hoe strangely around a place for the vacation

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the single letter supplied by 'a', holding it inside
the clue's letters are arranged strangely, so they must be shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily grips a garden hoe while out at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges I HOLD MY HOE into HOLIDYHOME, and 'around' wraps that round A, which slots in after HOLID.
explanation.definitionFit: A second residence kept for vacations is called by this name.

clue.text: She has to survive on nothing

definitions.note: a pronoun standing for any woman, here one with this given name

indicators.note: survive is placed on nothing, so the zero letter stands first with the living word after it

parts.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
to survive is to live

explanation.surface: A woman manages to get by with no money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for a girl's name, a common crossword convention, so the definition hides in the opening pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a female first name, so any 'she' could bear it.

clue.text: Live in a fashionable dress

parts.note: something fashionable is said to be in
a habit is a garment, as a nun's or a riding dress

explanation.surface: Someone spends all their time wearing one stylish outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live in' is the definition, not 'Live' alone: the two words together mean occupy.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a place as one's home is a straight synonym.

clue.text: One who is handsome and is crazy about love

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit about the zero, wrapped round it
the words 'and is' go crazy, so their letters are jumbled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, hence O

explanation.surface: A good-looking man is madly in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' scrambles AND IS to ADNIS, and 'about' puts it round O (love, the tennis nil) to give ADONIS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this youth was so beautiful his name became a byword for a good-looking man.

clue.text: Teacher on clothes and hat

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
gear is informal for clothing

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster pulls on his outfit and his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Headgear covers any hat, so the plain-looking last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat is one kind of covering worn on the head, the general term for such items.

clue.text: Enlarge a weight in a human being should Yankees start

indicators.note: the weight's letter goes in the word for a person, splitting it

parts.note: a man is a human being
G is short for gram, a unit of weight
'should you need help' means 'if you need help', so should can stand for if

indicators.note: the start of Yankees is its first letter

explanation.surface: A heavy load is growing on someone if American visitors begin to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the gram inside the person; 'should' means if, as in 'should it rain', and 'start' takes the first letter of Yankees.
explanation.definitionFit: To magnify is to make something look bigger, the sense of enlarge.

clue.text: Relative who turns aunt into discs

indicators.note: the words 'aunt into discs' turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some family member has a strange habit of changing an aunt into records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' signals that all thirteen letters of AUNT INTO DISCS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin far removed is still a member of the family, a relation.

clue.text: Person responsible for the highest achievement has to register a wave

definitions.text: Person responsible for the highest achievement

parts.note: to register something is to record it
a breaker is a wave that breaks on the shore

explanation.surface: A top performer must write down details of a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: The long opening phrase defines a person who beats the best mark so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets a new best mark in sport has achieved more than anyone before.

clue.text: People who are hard when following the flag

indicators.note: the letter for hard comes after the plant name

parts.note: the yellow flag is a wild iris, so flag names that plant
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Tough folk rally behind their national banner.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag is a plant name here, the iris that grows by water, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation of Ireland collectively: 'the Irish' is a people.

clue.text: Something refreshing in a poem about line and article

indicators.note: the poem goes about the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a range is a line, as of mountains or products
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A verse that mentions a line and an article proves refreshing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the poem round the line and article; range means line in the sense of a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fizzy citrus drink is a typical cooling beverage.

clue.text: In simple multiplication mathematics starts feeling shaky

indicators.note: the opening word puts the next letter in the multiplying word

parts.note: trebling is multiplying by three, about as simple as multiplying gets

indicators.note: the start of mathematics is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pupil gets nervous as arithmetic lessons begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal even though it opens the clue; 'starts' takes the first letter of mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quaking with nerves or cold is shaky.

clue.text: Times which sound all right for gentlemen

indicators.note: said aloud, the word suits titled gentlemen, so we want a word that is heard like theirs

parts.note: knights are gentlemen given the title Sir

explanation.surface: Some evenings out are fine for well-bred men.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of the evening hours sounds exactly like the titled men addressed as Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: Nights are periods of darkness, so they are times of day.

clue.text: One who spreads scandal when poser is confused by gravity

indicators.note: the gravity letter stands beside the jumbled words

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravity's acceleration

indicators.note: the words 'poser is' are confused, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter gets flustered by a solemn situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles POSER IS to OSSIPER, and G (gravity) stands by it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who passes on rumours and tittle-tattle is a tale-bearer.

clue.text: Female supporter

parts.note: not a fan but a carved woman holding up a building, a column in the shape of a draped female figure

explanation.definitionFit: In classical architecture a pillar carved as a robed woman bears the roof's weight.

clue.text: Violent weather on mountain, in charge of holding a risen man

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective meaning of a twister

indicators.note: the two outer pieces hold the turned name between them

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: in a down clue risen means the name reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Dan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A storm breaks over a hill while someone in command holds a man who has got up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risen' reverses the name because this is a down clue, and 'holding' puts it between hill and abbreviation. The definition is loose: the answer is the adjective from tornado.
explanation.definitionFit: Tornadic describes the most violent of storms, a whirling funnel of wind.

clue.text: Make a reservation after the event for a volume of records

indicators.note: the reserving word comes after the event word

parts.note: a case is an instance or event, as in 'in that case'
to book is to reserve a table or seat

explanation.surface: Someone books a seat after the fact and is sent a ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the reserving word second, though the clue gives it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A casebook is a bound log of a doctor's or detective's cases, a book of records.

clue.text: Left with a serpent — it has scales

indicators.note: the letter for left goes with the snake, side by side

parts.note: an adder is a snake

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck with a snake, which is covered in scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it has scales' looks like the snake again, but it is the definition: a ladder's rungs form a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaling a wall means climbing it, and a ladder's rungs are steps for climbing.

clue.text: Bit of a puzzle for a fault-finding creature

parts.note: to nag is to keep finding fault
a ram is a male sheep, a creature

explanation.surface: A carping beast is a little puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of a puzzle' is fair: in a crossword some clues are this kind of rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranged-letter wordplay is a standard component of crossword puzzles.

clue.text: Get better without the right one for the cup

indicators.note: without means outside here, so the healing word goes outside the other letters

parts.note: to cure is to heal, to make better
R is short for right
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone needs to recover before taking the trophy, without being right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: CURE goes round R and I. The Currie Cup is South Africa's domestic rugby (formerly also cricket) competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Currie Cup is the long-standing South African sporting trophy named after Sir Donald Currie.

clue.text: One is in a backward working-class society

indicators.note: one letter is in the other piece, sitting inside it
the class label is read backward

parts.note: non-U means not upper-class, the speech and habits of ordinary people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lone figure belongs to an old-fashioned group of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns NON-U into UNON, and 'is in' puts I inside to make the answer. U and non-U were 1950s British labels for upper-class and not upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A students' or trade association is a society of members.

clue.text: A real gun I exchange for a kind of pain

indicators.note: the letters exchange places, a rearrangement of the words

explanation.surface: Someone trades in a genuine firearm to buy relief from aches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges A REAL GUN I, nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is sharp nerve pain, a particular kind of ache.

clue.text: Spirits the information upon me twice

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the letter for 'me' appears two times

parts.note: I is the speaker, the subject form of me

explanation.surface: Ghosts give me the low-down twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii are jinn, supernatural beings of Arabian folklore, so spirits.

clue.text: A creature found inside one who finishes the cake, he comes from the north

indicators.note: the creature is found inside the cake decorator's word

parts.note: an icer puts the icing on a cake, the finishing touch
an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope turns up in a baker's kitchen; it hails from the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found inside' puts the antelope within the cake-decorator, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Iceland, the North Atlantic island near the Arctic Circle, comes from the north.

clue.text: Wash enjoyed by only one miner in seven

indicators.note: the word is held by just one stretch of the words that follow, lying inside them

explanation.surface: Of seven mining dwarfs, only one ever takes a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'mineR IN SEven'; the surface pictures the seven dwarfs of the fairy tale, who were miners.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash out with clean water.

clue.text: Mother on the river held by child to be a servant

indicators.note: the river and mother are held by the child, inside its letters

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: mother comes on after the river in this across clue

parts.note: the Itchen is a river in Hampshire, flowing through Winchester
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother on a riverbank clutched by her toddler becomes the hired help.
explanation.walkthrough: The child is split open after its first letter to hold the river and mother; the Itchen is a chalk stream in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid who works in the kitchen is a domestic servant.
